figures.caption: Table 1: Nodes of each data set and how they are obtained.

Figure 1: RMGC. Inputs (left): the signals at their own rates, grouped by the level that matches their sampling rate. Models (middle): each signal is predicted at its level by its own least-squares model; every model uses causal windows of all signals’ own past samples, and the power of fast signals. Output (right): one directed graph, with an edge u → v when u’s block of regressors is significant for v (F test per source, Benjamini–Hochberg over the pairs), within or across timescales; the edges shown are an example. The hidden-driver attack (bottom) takes each declared edge and returns its robustness value.

Table 2: The matched comparison: the grid methods with EEG power columns and one test per pair (Bonferroni over each pair’s grids and columns, then one Benjamini–Hochberg procedure over the 36 pairs), without power, and the RMGC variants (64 replicates). ∗Outside the volume-conduction scenario.

Figure 2: Recall against false-positive rate in each of the 64 benchmark replicates, for RMGC and the established methods given the same EEG power features and one test per pair. Large markers: means. Dotted line: a false-positive rate of 0.05.

Figure 3: Example graphs. Colours: blue, true edges and red, false edges (b, c); green, stable edges and orange, breathing-sensitive edges (d); grey dotted, edges from breathing; grey dashed, the hidden arousal (a). (a) True graph of the nonlinear-edge scenario. (b) Edges declared by the union of common grids in one replicate, and (c) by RMGC-NN in the same replicate, with robustness values. (d) One deep-NREM segment of recording n1: edges from breathing in the run with breathing, and the edges of the hidden-breathing run with their breathing multiples k.

Figure 4: (a) Robustness values of true and faked edges in the benchmark (RMGC). (b) Breathing multiples of the same edges where breathing was observed; dotted line: as strong as breathing. (c) Sleep, (d) BBBD and (e) MultiPhysio-HRC: breathing multiples of the brain–heart edges of the runs without breathing, stable and breathing-sensitive. Black bars: medians.
